newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Market dazzles but pressure seen.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Market dazzles but pressure seen.

text.p: U.S. stock staged a dramatic turnaround from steep early losses but the action did not convince all participants a full-fledged recovery was at hand.

Jay Shartsis, head of options trading at R.F. Lafferty & Co, and Jerry Hegarty, an analyst at Thomson Financial Services, both noted that investor bullishness, as measured by a heavy amount of call buying this week, suggests the market may be in for more trouble over the near term.
But by about 1400 CDT/1900 GMT, the bellwether Dow industrial average was down only nine points at 7,321 after dropping more than 88 points in early action.
"It was a huge rally, but from here, I'm not sure it's back to business as usual," Shartsis said. "The put/call complex is not particularly good."
Among other stock indices, the S&P 100 was down 2.87 at 824.45 after falling to 812.68 and the S&P 500 was ahead 0.99 at 845.07. It had dropped to 831.87.
June S&P 500 futures were up 1.40 at 846.90. It reached a session low of 831.50.
The market got off to a rocky start after technology leader Intel Corp warned its second quarter revenues and net income would fall short of expectations.
Intel shares slumped to 140, down more than 23 points off the opening bell. It had recovered to 150-3/4, down 13-1/64 in afternoon trade. Volume was extremely heavy at more than 50 million shares.
Traders said Intel options were very busy as investors reacted to the stock's decline.
"Early on we had a lot of put sellers in there," said one Intel options trader. "Now it's just looking for some level where it can hang out for a while."
He added that investors were busy in all expiration months.
"I would suspect that people are trying to hedge their long positions by going out to the October and January options," he said.
Hegarty said Intel's sharp opening drop would likely have lingering effects, even if the market stabilizes.

"I don't think you just see a down open and that's the end of a move," he said. "You start talking about a leader like Intel being down 20 points, you would think that would lead to some temporary alarm.
"There is no fear in this market which will eventually be the death of the market when it comes," he added.
On the sentiment side, Shartsis said one new survey he saw showed 69 percent bullishness.
"When this rally started, that was about a 32," he said. "I wouldn't buy them (stocks) here."
But he also marveled at the recovery.
"The bottom line to all of this is that the market really is amazing and its behaviour is different than I've ever seen," Hegarty said.
He said first-of-the-month buying could provide support early next week "but I wouldn't disregard what I've seen today."
